source_excerpt: The 2026 US midterm elections are shaping up to be a significant test of Indian-American political representation.Four Indian-origin Democrats â Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam â are seeking re-election to the House of Representatives. The outcomes could determine not only which party controls Capitol Hill but also how much influence Indian-American lawmakers exercise in Washington and state governments.Indian-Americans in key congressional races1. Before entering Congress, he taught economics at Stanford University, practised law and served as deputy assistant secretary of commerce under President Barack Obama.He now sits on the House Armed Services Committee and has been an influential voice on issues ranging from artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing to US competition with China.Read also | US midterms 2026: Meet Ro Khanna, Indian-American Congressman behind Epstein files pushKhanna has been a vocal critic of President Donald Trump, particularly over his economic policies, immigration crackdown and approach to democratic institutions. Pramila JayapalPramila Jayapal is seeking re-election from Washingtonâs 7th Congressional District, which includes much of Seattle and surrounding communities. Before entering electoral politics, she founded OneAmerica, a Washington-based immigrant-rights organisation, and became a prominent campaigner for immigration reform and civil liberties. Her experience as an activist has shaped her legislative priorities, particularly on deportations, detention, family separation and pathways to legal status.Jayapal has championed Medicare for All, stronger labour protections, affordable housing, climate action and expanded access to education.
